business: MyLiquid Gate (runtime controls for AI agents at brokers, crypto venues and neobanks)
target: the person who would sign for agent controls (head of product, CTO or chief compliance officer) at a US mid-size broker, crypto venue or neobank that opened, or plans to open, customer accounts to AI agents
where: United States, sold online and through design partners
_sources: Segments from docs/discovery/1-problem-and-audience.md (segment D) and docs/startup/plan.md (who buys, in order). Objections from founder/board.md and founder/competitors.md. Segment shares, salary ranges and behaviour shares are estimates, not data; no interviews have been done yet.

behaviours.name: Builds in-house by default
behaviours.how: Has an engineering team and buys only what it cannot build in a quarter.

behaviours.name: Compliance-led
behaviours.how: Buys when an examiner, auditor or regulator asks a question the firm cannot answer.

behaviours.name: Waits for regulation
behaviours.how: Acts on written rules and enforcement actions, not on reports and speeches.

behaviours.name: Fast follower
behaviours.how: Watches what Robinhood and Coinbase do and copies it within two quarters.

behaviours.name: Vendor-risk cautious
behaviours.how: Every vendor in the trade path needs a SOC 2 report, references and a security review.

behaviours.name: Budget-squeezed
behaviours.how: Every new tool competes with headcount; prefers free tiers and open source.

behaviours.name: Early adopter
behaviours.how: Likes being first and will run a pilot with a startup if it moves fast.

objections: I won't put a startup without a SOC 2 report in our order path
Our agent volume is tiny today
Our terms already put agent risk on the customer
Another hop in the order path means latency and a new point of failure
Why would I trust an identity registry the vendor's founder started?
Per-action pricing is hard to budget
